title: Minimum Number of Flips to Reverse Binary String
summary: Given a positive integer n , let s be its binary representation without leading zeros.
statement: Given a positive integer n , let s be its binary representation without leading zeros. The reverse of s is obtained by writing the characters of s in the opposite order. You can flip any bit in s (change 0 to 1 or 1 to 0), and each flip affects exactly one bit. Determine the minimum number of flips required to make s equal to its reverse.
constraints: Write positive n in binary without leading zeros.
Flip individual bits until the string equals its reversal.
Return the minimum number of flips.
hints: Compare mirrored positions only through half the bit string.
A matching pair needs no work.
A mismatched pair needs exactly one flip on either side.
Different mirrored pairs are independent, so their mismatch count is minimal.
editorial: Different mirrored pairs are independent, so their mismatch count is minimal.

tests.explanation: Binary 111 is already symmetric, so zero flips are required.
Binary 1010 has two mismatched mirrored pairs, requiring two flips.
